title: compact-latency-slipstream-sdk-guidelines
content:
Summary:

This note captures an experiment-first PRD for a low-latency streaming surface that combines compact delta frames, speculative tool priming, and an ergonomic SDK that surfaces progressive structured output while keeping payload overhead minimal. "Slipstream" is our working name for the pattern: lightweight speculative priming + compact frames + resumable streams to shave tens-to-hundreds of ms from median end-to-end latencies for mobile/edge clients and busy server-side flows.

Why this? Problem statement:
- Many hosted-api customers complain about tail latency spikes when tool-calling is involved (db lookups, external api) despite our good token latency.
- SDKs today either expose byte-heavy JSON patches for partial structured output (good for debugging, bad for bandwidth) or opaque protoframes (good bandwidth, poor developer ergonomics).
- When a tool is expected, clients block while the model produces the tool instruction then we make a separate call. That round-trip kills interactive feel.

High-level goals:
- Provide an SDK-first surface that lets apps see meaningful partial structured results immediately (progressive JSON-lite) while supporting speculative tool priming to reduce perceived tool latency.
- Keep wire bytes small: prefer compact delta frames (binary-friendly but human-checkable) over repeated full JSON blobs.
- Make streams resumable and backpressure-aware so mobile reconnections and flaky networks don't require full reruns.
- Offer straightforward telemetry hooks for cost/latency attribution per-frame and per-tool-call.

Non-goals (for this cycle):
- Full formal schema evolution system — we'll rely on lightweight version tags in frames and leave heavy schema migration later.
- Rewriting existing SDKs' entire ergonomics; start with JS + Python minimal surfaces.

Core ideas and components:
1) Compact delta frame format
- Frame types: META (session metadata), DELTA (small structural update), TOOL_HINT (model signals intent to call tool), TOOL_RESULT (tool response embedded or referenced), COMMIT (final structured payload), CHECKPOINT (resumable snapshot).
- Each DELTA is a small patch: {path, op, val} encoded in compact newline-separated jsonl-ish text; servers can compress/quantize before transport.
- We intentionally keep the representation inspectable for debugging: tools can log deltas server-side and replay into SDK to rebuild state.

2) Speculative tool priming (speculation lanes)
- When model emits TOOL_HINT, the runtime can optionally (policy-controlled) begin speculatively priming known tool endpoints (DNS preconnect, warm lambda, cached DB query) in parallel.
- SDKs receive TOOL_HINT frame and can surface a UI hint like: "Fetching context...". If priming succeeds, overall perceived time to tool result reduces significantly.
- Priming policy: configurable per-customer and route (allow/disallow speculation for sensitive operations). Default: enabled for non-sensitive, short-lived tool calls.

3) Resumable streams and checkpoints
- Periodic CHECKPOINT frames carry a compact snapshot id and minimal metadata (last-commit-id, sequence number, model-version). Clients can reconnect and request resume from a checkpoint id rather than re-running entire prompt.
- SDK exposes resume() on network errors that attaches last-checkpoint-id to new requests. Backend validates checkpoint TTL and accepts resume if still warm.

4) SDK ergonomics (JS + Python prototypes)
- Goal: expose a tiny, idiomatic API surface that hides frames unless developers opt-in for structured deltas.
- Minimal JS pseudocode:
  const s = client.stream({model: 'rwd-stream-1', prompt});
  s.on('delta', (patch) => applyPatchToState(patch));
  s.on('tool_hint', (hint) => prewarm(hint));
  s.on('commit', (obj) => renderFinal(obj));
  // automatic resume on unstable networks if checkpoint present

- Default high-level convenience: client.partialRender(callback) reconstructs object state from DELTA frames and forwards tidy structured blob every N ms for easy React binding.
- Advanced: rawFrameStream() for debugging and low-level flow control.

5) Observability and billing signals
- Emit per-frame telemetry: frame_type, seq, token_count_estimate, downstream-tool-id (nullable), latency_ms (wallclock on server send), bytes.
- Aggregate metrics: speculative-priming-success-rate, resume-hit-rate, average delta-merge-time (client), median perceived-tool-latency.

Operational constraints and safety:
- Speculation must be opt-in per customer and per-route; we cannot speculatively send sensitive PII to third-party tools. Documented gating and policy enforcement required.
- Checkpoints TTL and storage cost: short default TTL (5m) to avoid indefinite retention; premium customers can opt for longer resume windows.

Backwards compatibility and migration strategy:
- New endpoint: /stream/slipstream-v1 (clearly versioned). Existing /stream endpoints unchanged.
- SDKs default to not parsing compact DELTA frames unless developer calls client.enableDeltaParsing(). This keeps existing clients unaffected.
- Launch flow: alpha with internal teams -> small pilot customers (eng-sre, solutions-eng) -> gradual opt-in.

Testing and success criteria:
- Perf: target 15–50% reduction in median perceived tool latency for pilot workloads.
- Bandwidth: target <2x bandwidth delta vs current incremental JSON approach for equivalent application workloads.
- Developer ergonomics: pilot teams can integrate partialRender in under ~3 hours with existing codebase.

Rollout and milestones (rough):
- Q1: Prototyping and SDK minimal API + internal alpha (runtime + small UI demo app).
- Q2: Instrumentation + safety policy gating + pilot customers.
- Q3: GA with console toggles, billing flags, and public docs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent complex array diffs compactly without making deltas unreadable? (Liam to spike)
- Circuit breaker semantics for speculative priming: how aggressive? How many concurrent primed tools per session?
- Resume trust model: how to ensure checkpoint replay doesn't expose stale or revoked data?

Notes to self / friction bits:
- SDK convenience vs explicitness trade: too much magic (auto merge) might hide hard bugs — keep raw API available.
- UX: we should prototype a tiny web demo that visually shows deltas being applied — helps PM/UX sell idea.

Appendix: quick implementation sketch (runtime hooks):
- When model emits tool intent token, runtime emits TOOL_HINT frame with tool-id + minimal param sketch (hash or non-sensitive preview).
- Router consults priming policy: if allowed, call governance layer to start prewarm async; mark telemetry.
- If tool completes and result is safe, server emits TOOL_RESULT. If tool is external and cannot be included, emit TOOL_REF with id and instructions for SDK to fetch via secure client endpoint.

Relevant tickets / links:
- INF-2248: slipstream prototype tracking (see linked_artifacts)
- runtime PR 789: delta frame encoder WIP

If this direction seems valuable, next concrete step: Liam/Marco to produce a 2-day spike that implements JS SDK applyPatch prototype + a tiny server that streams artificially generated DELTA frames + PR with example app. Sophie to draft security policy summary for priming.

-- end of note --
